# Discharge Checklist (synthetic, POL-GEN-01 companion)
1. Discharge diagnoses listed (primary first).
2. Medication list reproduced exactly as ordered (POL-MED-08) - no changes, additions or omissions.
3. High-risk medications highlighted with education points (anticoagulant, insulin, opioid, antiplatelet).
4. Readmission-risk tier computed (LACE, POL-RISK-02) with contributing factors stated.
5. Follow-up appointments proposed inside the policy windows, each citing its policy section.
6. Home-care / equipment / transportation needs addressed (POL-HOME-07).
7. Red-flag return precautions included.
8. Transitional-care phone call scheduled when required by risk tier or partial teach-back.
9. Plan marked DRAFT until a licensed clinician approves it; HIGH risk requires explicit approval.


POLICY EXCERPTS:
[general_discharge_policy.md#primary-care-follow-up] Every discharged adult must have a primary care (PCP) follow-up visit scheduled within 7 to 14 days of discharge. Patients with a high readmission-risk tier must be seen within 7 days.
[pulmonary_followup_policy.md#copd-exacerbation] Patients discharged after a COPD exacerbation require a follow-up visit (pulmonology or PCP) within 7 days. Inhaler technique must be re-checked at that visit. Refer to pulmonary rehabilitation within 4 weeks of discharge. Patients discharged on new home oxygen need an oxygen re-assessment within 30 to 60 days.
[readmission_risk_protocols.md#actions-by-tier] HIGH risk: clinician approval of the discharge plan is mandatory before finalization; transitional-care phone call within 48 hours; PCP or specialist visit within 7 days; consider home health referral. MEDIUM risk: phone call within 72 hours; follow-up within 7 to 14 days. LOW risk: standard follow-up within 14 days.
[home_care_policy.md#home-health-referral-eligibility] Refer to home health nursing when the patient is homebound or has a HIGH readmission-risk tier and lives alone, needs medication-management support, has new home oxygen, or has new injectable medications and no trained caregiver.
[home_care_policy.md#transportation] Patients with no transportation must be offered transportation assistance for every follow-up appointment, or a telehealth visit where clinically appropriate.
[general_discharge_policy.md#clinical-orders] The discharge planning process must never alter clinical orders. Any suspected discrepancy or requested change in medications, doses, or treatments is routed to the responsible clinician for decision.
[cardiology_followup_policy.md#heart-failure] Patients discharged after a heart failure admission require a cardiology or heart-failure clinic visit within 7 days of discharge. Daily weights must be taught; instruct the patient to report a weight gain of more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week. Basic metabolic panel (potassium and creatinine) within 7 days when a diuretic, mineralocorticoid antagonist, or ARNI was started or changed.
[home_care_policy.md#durable-medical-equipment] New home oxygen, walkers, and shower chairs must be ordered and delivery confirmed before discharge. Patients living on an upper floor without an elevator need a home-safety assessment.

CHECKLIST:
# Discharge Checklist (synthetic, POL-GEN-01 companion)
1. Discharge diagnoses listed (primary first).
2. Medication list reproduced exactly as ordered (POL-MED-08) - no changes, additions or omissions.
3. High-risk medications highlighted with education points (anticoagulant, insulin, opioid, antiplatelet).
4. Readmission-risk tier computed (LACE, POL-RISK-02) with contributing factors stated.
5. Follow-up appointments proposed inside the policy windows, each citing its policy section.
6. Home-care / equipment / transportation needs addressed (POL-HOME-07).
7. Red-flag return precautions included.
8. Transitional-care phone call scheduled when required by risk tier or partial teach-back.
9. Plan marked DRAFT until a licensed clinician approves it; HIGH risk requires explicit approval.


POLICY EXCERPTS:
[general_discharge_policy.md#primary-care-follow-up] Every discharged adult must have a primary care (PCP) follow-up visit scheduled within 7 to 14 days of discharge. Patients with a high readmission-risk tier must be seen within 7 days.
[pulmonary_followup_policy.md#community-acquired-pneumonia] Patients discharged after community-acquired pneumonia require a PCP visit within 14 days. A follow-up chest X-ray at 6 weeks is recommended only for patients over 50 years or smokers. Patients must complete the full antibiotic course as ordered.
[readmission_risk_protocols.md#actions-by-tier] HIGH risk: clinician approval of the discharge plan is mandatory before finalization; transitional-care phone call within 48 hours; PCP or specialist visit within 7 days; consider home health referral. MEDIUM risk: phone call within 72 hours; follow-up within 7 to 14 days. LOW risk: standard follow-up within 14 days.
[general_discharge_policy.md#clinical-orders] The discharge planning process must never alter clinical orders. Any suspected discrepancy or requested change in medications, doses, or treatments is routed to the responsible clinician for decision.
[home_care_policy.md#home-health-referral-eligibility] Refer to home health nursing when the patient is homebound or has a HIGH readmission-risk tier and lives alone, needs medication-management support, has new home oxygen, or has new injectable medications and no trained caregiver.
[pulmonary_followup_policy.md#copd-exacerbation] Patients discharged after a COPD exacerbation require a follow-up visit (pulmonology or PCP) within 7 days. Inhaler technique must be re-checked at that visit. Refer to pulmonary rehabilitation within 4 weeks of discharge. Patients discharged on new home oxygen need an oxygen re-assessment within 30 to 60 days.
[pulmonary_followup_policy.md#red-flag-symptoms] Worsening breathlessness at rest, SpO2 below 88% on home oxygen, confusion, or fever returning after antibiotics require urgent review.
[general_discharge_policy.md#discharge-plan-contents] A discharge plan must contain: discharge diagnoses, the reconciled medication list exactly as ordered, follow-up appointments with target windows, home-care or equipment needs, return precautions (red-flag symptoms), and the name of the responsible clinician. The plan is a draft until a licensed clinician approves it.

According to policy, a heart failure patient discharged after an admission must be seen in a cardiology or heart-failure clinic within 7 days of discharge [cardiology_followup_policy.md#heart-failure]. 

Regarding labs, a basic metabolic panel (specifically checking potassium and creatinine) is required within 7 days if a diuretic, mineralocorticoid antagonist, or ARNI was started or changed [cardiology_followup_policy.md#heart-failure].

[general_discharge_policy.md#primary-care-follow-up] Every discharged adult must have a primary care (PCP) follow-up visit scheduled within 7 to 14 days of discharge. Patients with a high readmission-risk tier must be seen within 7 days.
[pulmonary_followup_policy.md#copd-exacerbation] Patients discharged after a COPD exacerbation require a follow-up visit (pulmonology or PCP) within 7 days. [readmission_risk_protocols.md#actions-by-tier] HIGH risk: clinician approval of the discharge plan is mandatory before finalization; transitional-care phone call within 48 hours; PCP or specialist visit within 7 days; consider home health referral. [home_care_policy.md#home-health-referral-eligibility] Refer to home health nursing when the patient is homebound or has a HIGH readmission-risk tier and lives alone, needs medication-management support, has new home oxygen, or has new injectable medications and no trained caregiver.
[home_care_policy.md#transportation] Patients with no transportation must be offered transportation assistance for every follow-up appointment, or a telehealth visit where clinically appropriate.
[general_discharge_policy.md#clinical-orders] The discharge planning process must never alter clinical orders. Any suspected discrepancy or requested change in medications, doses, or treatments is routed to the responsible clinician for decision.
[general_discharge_policy.md#teach-back] Discharge education must use teach-back. If teach-back is only partially successful, schedule a transitional-care phone call within 48 to 72 hours.
[cardiology_followup_policy.md#heart-failure] Patients discharged after a heart failure admission require a cardiology or heart-failure clinic visit within 7 days of discharge. Daily weights must be taught; instruct the patient to report a weight gain of more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week. Basic metabolic panel (potassium and creatinine) within 7 days when a diuretic, mineralocorticoid antagonist, or ARNI was started or changed.

[general_discharge_policy.md#primary-care-follow-up] Every discharged adult must have a primary care (PCP) follow-up visit scheduled within 7 to 14 days of discharge. Patients with a high readmission-risk tier must be seen within 7 days.
[pulmonary_followup_policy.md#copd-exacerbation] Patients discharged after a COPD exacerbation require a follow-up visit (pulmonology or PCP) within 7 days. [general_discharge_policy.md#teach-back] Discharge education must use teach-back. If teach-back is only partially successful, schedule a transitional-care phone call within 48 to 72 hours.

[home_care_policy.md#transportation] Patients with no transportation must be offered transportation assistance for every follow-up appointment, or a telehealth visit where clinically appropriate.

[home_care_policy.md#durable-medical-equipment] New home oxygen, walkers, and shower chairs must be ordered and delivery confirmed before discharge. Patients living on an upper floor without an elevator need a home-safety assessment.

[home_care_policy.md#durable-medical-equipment] New home oxygen, walkers, and shower chairs must be ordered and delivery confirmed before discharge. Patients living on an upper floor without an elevator need a home-safety assessment.
[general_discharge_policy.md#teach-back] Discharge education must use teach-back. If teach-back is only partially successful, schedule a transitional-care phone call within 48 to 72 hours.

2. Medication list reproduced exactly as ordered (POL-MED-08) - no changes, additions or omissions.
3. High-risk medications highlighted with education points (anticoagulant, insulin, opioid, antiplatelet).
4. Readmission-risk tier computed (LACE, POL-RISK-02) with contributing factors stated.
5. Follow-up appointments proposed inside the policy windows, each citing its policy section.
6. Home-care / equipment / transportation needs addressed (POL-HOME-07).
7. Red-flag return precautions included.
8. Transitional-care phone call scheduled when required by risk tier or partial teach-back.
9. Plan marked DRAFT until a licensed clinician approves it; HIGH risk requires explicit approval.


POLICY EXCERPTS:
[general_discharge_policy.md#primary-care-follow-up] Every discharged adult must have a primary care (PCP) follow-up visit scheduled within 7 to 14 days of discharge. Patients with a high readmission-risk tier must be seen within 7 days.
[orthopedic_followup_policy.md#total-joint-arthroplasty] Patients discharged after total hip or knee arthroplasty require a wound check at 10 to 14 days and a surgeon follow-up visit at 6 weeks. Outpatient or home physical therapy must start within 3 days of discharge. VTE prophylaxis continues for the ordered duration and must not be stopped early without the surgeon.
[readmission_risk_protocols.md#actions-by-tier] HIGH risk: clinician approval of the discharge plan is mandatory before finalization; transitional-care phone call within 48 hours; PCP or specialist visit within 7 days; consider home health referral. MEDIUM risk: phone call within 72 hours; follow-up within 7 to 14 days. LOW risk: standard follow-up within 14 days.
[medication_reconciliation_policy.md#high-risk-medications] Anticoagulants, insulin, opioids and antiplatelet agents at discharge require specific patient education and must be highlighted in the plan.
[general_discharge_policy.md#clinical-orders] The discharge planning process must never alter clinical orders. Any suspected discrepancy or requested change in medications, doses, or treatments is routed to the responsible clinician for decision.
[home_care_policy.md#durable-medical-equipment] New home oxygen, walkers, and shower chairs must be ordered and delivery confirmed before discharge. Patients living on an upper floor without an elevator need a home-safety assessment.
[medication_reconciliation_policy.md#discrepancies-and-requested-changes] Any discrepancy, or any request to change a medication or dose, is escalated to the prescribing clinician and is never actioned by the copilot. The plan remains in draft until resolved.
[medication_reconciliation_policy.md#reconciliation-rule] The discharge medication list must be reproduced exactly as ordered by the prescriber: drug, dose, route, frequency. Automated tools and copilots may format or group the list but must not change, add, omit, or substitute any medication.

[cardiology_followup_policy.md#heart-failure] Patients discharged after a heart failure admission require a cardiology or heart-failure clinic visit within 7 days of discharge. Daily weights must be taught; instruct the patient to report a weight gain of more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week. Basic metabolic panel (potassium and creatinine) within 7 days when a diuretic, mineralocorticoid antagonist, or ARNI was started or changed.
[pulmonary_followup_policy.md#community-acquired-pneumonia] Patients discharged after community-acquired pneumonia require a PCP visit within 14 days. A follow-up chest X-ray at 6 weeks is recommended only for patients over 50 years or smokers. Patients must complete the full antibiotic course as ordered.
[medication_reconciliation_policy.md#discrepancies-and-requested-changes] Any discrepancy, or any request to change a medication or dose, is escalated to the prescribing clinician and is never actioned by the copilot. The plan remains in draft until resolved.

    "Take ticagrelor 90 mg by mouth twice daily and do not stop it without talking to your cardiologist.",
    "Take atorvastatin 80 mg by mouth once daily for cholesterol control.",
    "Take metoprolol tartrate 25 mg by mouth twice daily; monitor your heart rate and do not skip doses.",
    "If you have chest pain, use nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingually; you may repeat every 5 minutes up to a total of three doses, then call 911 if pain continues.",
    "Schedule a cardiology appointment within 14 days, a primary‑care visit within 7‑14 days, and begin cardiac‑rehabilitation as arranged before discharge."

  "red_flags": [
    "New or worsening chest pain or pressure.",
    "Shortness of breath at rest or with minimal activity.",
    "Feeling light‑headed, fainting, or having rapid/pounding heartbeats.",
    "Any signs of bleeding such as unusual bruising, nosebleeds, blood in stool or urine, or black/tarry stools.",
    "Sudden swelling of the legs or rapid weight gain."
  ]
}

QUESTION: Per the pulmonary policy, how soon after a COPD exacerbation must she be seen, and when is the rehab referral due?
PATIENT CONTEXT: COPD with acute exacerbation Chronic diastolic heart failure
EXCERPTS:
[general_discharge_policy.md#primary-care-follow-up] Every discharged adult must have a primary care (PCP) follow-up visit scheduled within 7 to 14 days of discharge. Patients with a high readmission-risk tier must be seen within 7 days.
[pulmonary_followup_policy.md#copd-exacerbation] Patients discharged after a COPD exacerbation require a follow-up visit (pulmonology or PCP) within 7 days. Inhaler technique must be re-checked at that visit. Refer to pulmonary rehabilitation within 4 weeks of discharge. Patients discharged on new home oxygen need an oxygen re-assessment within 30 to 60 days.
[readmission_risk_protocols.md#actions-by-tier] HIGH risk: clinician approval of the discharge plan is mandatory before finalization; transitional-care phone call within 48 hours; PCP or specialist visit within 7 days; consider home health referral. MEDIUM risk: phone call within 72 hours; follow-up within 7 to 14 days. LOW risk: standard follow-up within 14 days.
[home_care_policy.md#home-health-referral-eligibility] Refer to home health nursing when the patient is homebound or has a HIGH readmission-risk tier and lives alone, needs medication-management support, has new home oxygen, or has new injectable medications and no trained caregiver.
[home_care_policy.md#transportation] Patients with no transportation must be offered transportation assistance for every follow-up appointment, or a telehealth visit where clinically appropriate.
[general_discharge_policy.md#clinical-orders] The discharge planning process must never alter clinical orders. Any suspected discrepancy or requested change in medications, doses, or treatments is routed to the responsible clinician for decision.
[cardiology_followup_policy.md#heart-failure] Patients discharged after a heart failure admission require a cardiology or heart-failure clinic visit within 7 days of discharge. Daily weights must be taught; instruct the patient to report a weight gain of more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week. Basic metabolic panel (potassium and creatinine) within 7 days when a diuretic, mineralocorticoid antagonist, or ARNI was started or changed.
[home_care_policy.md#durable-medical-equipment] New home oxygen, walkers, and shower chairs must be ordered and delivery confirmed before discharge. Patients living on an upper floor without an elevator need a home-safety assessment.

PATIENT CONTEXT: Type 1 diabetes with diabetic ketoacidosis
EXCERPTS:
[general_discharge_policy.md#primary-care-follow-up] Every discharged adult must have a primary care (PCP) follow-up visit scheduled within 7 to 14 days of discharge. Patients with a high readmission-risk tier must be seen within 7 days.
[endocrine_followup_policy.md#diabetic-ketoacidosis] Patients discharged after diabetic ketoacidosis require an endocrinology or diabetes-clinic visit within 7 days and a diabetes-educator session within 14 days. A glucagon rescue kit must be prescribed and the caregiver taught how to use it. Sick-day rules must be taught before discharge.
[readmission_risk_protocols.md#actions-by-tier] HIGH risk: clinician approval of the discharge plan is mandatory before finalization; transitional-care phone call within 48 hours; PCP or specialist visit within 7 days; consider home health referral. MEDIUM risk: phone call within 72 hours; follow-up within 7 to 14 days. LOW risk: standard follow-up within 14 days.
[medication_reconciliation_policy.md#high-risk-medications] Anticoagulants, insulin, opioids and antiplatelet agents at discharge require specific patient education and must be highlighted in the plan.
[general_discharge_policy.md#clinical-orders] The discharge planning process must never alter clinical orders. Any suspected discrepancy or requested change in medications, doses, or treatments is routed to the responsible clinician for decision.

QUESTION: What does the diabetes policy require for follow-up after DKA?
PATIENT CONTEXT: Type 1 diabetes with diabetic ketoacidosis
EXCERPTS:
[general_discharge_policy.md#primary-care-follow-up] Every discharged adult must have a primary care (PCP) follow-up visit scheduled within 7 to 14 days of discharge. Patients with a high readmission-risk tier must be seen within 7 days.
[endocrine_followup_policy.md#diabetic-ketoacidosis] Patients discharged after diabetic ketoacidosis require an endocrinology or diabetes-clinic visit within 7 days and a diabetes-educator session within 14 days. A glucagon rescue kit must be prescribed and the caregiver taught how to use it. Sick-day rules must be taught before discharge.
[readmission_risk_protocols.md#actions-by-tier] HIGH risk: clinician approval of the discharge plan is mandatory before finalization; transitional-care phone call within 48 hours; PCP or specialist visit within 7 days; consider home health referral. MEDIUM risk: phone call within 72 hours; follow-up within 7 to 14 days. LOW risk: standard follow-up within 14 days.
[medication_reconciliation_policy.md#high-risk-medications] Anticoagulants, insulin, opioids and antiplatelet agents at discharge require specific patient education and must be highlighted in the plan.
[general_discharge_policy.md#clinical-orders] The discharge planning process must never alter clinical orders. Any suspected discrepancy or requested change in medications, doses, or treatments is routed to the responsible clinician for decision.
[endocrine_followup_policy.md#red-flag-symptoms] Vomiting that prevents eating or drinking, blood glucose above 300 mg/dL on two readings, or ketones moderate or higher require same-day contact with the diabetes team or emergency care.
[medication_reconciliation_policy.md#discrepancies-and-requested-changes] Any discrepancy, or any request to change a medication or dose, is escalated to the prescribing clinician and is never actioned by the copilot. The plan remains in draft until resolved.
[medication_reconciliation_policy.md#reconciliation-rule] The discharge medication list must be reproduced exactly as ordered by the prescriber: drug, dose, route, frequency. Automated tools and copilots may format or group the list but must not change, add, omit, or substitute any medication.
